Optimal.Notes: A locked 40 fps at 40 Hz refresh feels noticeably smoother than 30 and is a great sweet spot for this game's fast-paced combat. Textures at Medium preserve monster detail while shadows stay Low to protect the GPU budget in dense areas.

profiles.Summary: Monster Hunter: World runs on the Steam Deck at a playable level, though its demanding open-world environments and dense foliage push the hardware — expect 30-40 fps with tuned settings rather than a locked 60. The game is Steam Deck Verified and ProtonDB reporters trend platinum, so compatibility is solid with no major launch blockers.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs (the Deck's GPU sits between the minimum GTX 760 and recommended GTX 1060 tiers), the game's ProtonDB gold/platinum trend, and the Deck's hardware capabilities. On first run, check frame rate in the Ancient Forest canopy — if it dips below your target, drop Shadow Quality to Low and reduce Image Quality by 10-15 points.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render resolution dropped to 960x600 with FSR upscaling to ease GPU load; TDP cap of 8 W keeps thermals and fan noise low for handheld sessions. Foliage and shadows are the biggest power draws — keeping both at Low is essential here.

KnownIssues: Anti-cheat (Denuvo) has historically caused occasional stutters on first launch; subsequent runs are smoother
Online multiplayer sessions can cause additional frame drops in populated areas
High-density areas (Ancient Forest canopy, Coral Highlands) are the most demanding zones and may dip below target fps
Some users report needing to set the game to Windowed Fullscreen to avoid resolution/display issues under Proton

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 at uncapped TDP gives the best visual fidelity the Deck can produce, but 60 fps is not consistently achievable — expect drops into the 40s in foliage-heavy zones. Consider dropping Shadow Quality to Low if stutters appear in the Ancient Forest.

Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh rate and frame cap deliver a smooth, tear-free feel that balances visual quality with stable performance. FSR upscaling from 1024x640 recovers sharpness while keeping GPU headroom for consistent framing.

profiles.Summary: Monster Hunter: World runs well on the Steam Deck OLED, landing between the minimum and recommended PC GPU specs — expect stable 30 fps at low-to-medium settings with FSR upscaling, and up to 45 fps in lighter scenes at max performance. The game is Steam Deck Verified and ProtonDB reports trend platinum, so out-of-the-box compatibility under the default Proton version is generally solid.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended GPU specs relative to the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU class. On first run, check frame rate in Astera (the busiest hub area) and during a large monster fight — if it dips heavily, drop to the Optimal or Max Battery profile.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 and upscaling with Deck FSR keeps GPU load minimal; the 8 W TDP and 900 MHz GPU clock stretch battery life as far as possible. Expect occasional dips below 30 fps in Astera or during large multi-monster fights.

KnownIssues: Stuttering and frame dips can occur in Astera hub and during multi-monster encounters due to CPU/GPU saturation at higher settings.
The game defaults to high render resolution and high quality settings on first launch — manual adjustment is strongly recommended before playing.
Online multiplayer can exhibit occasional connectivity issues under Proton, though most players report it works.
TAA anti-aliasing causes noticeable blurring at sub-native resolutions; disabling it and using Deck FSR upscaling instead is recommended.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 at medium settings pushes the Deck GPU hard; expect 50+ fps in open fields but drops into the low 40s in Astera and during intense multi-monster fights — lower Shadow Quality to Low if dips are too frequent.
